doc.title: Greg Caputo interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 14, 1998

chapter: Playing styles, cruises and tribute bands
title: Advice on not showing off in a gig
summary: Better to be asked for more than less, and let others ask you for a solo.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Good advice. Something that can you verbalize this — well we talked about this, trying to verbalize that to students, that a gig is perhaps not for you to show all your chops off. Maybe you’ll get your moment at some point to do that, but—

It’s much better to be asked to play louder than softer. It’s much better to be asked to play a little more than a little less. And these are tools that I’ve used throughout my career, and invaluable, and I convey that to my students. You know you’ll get your chance, don’t ask for a drum solo, let them ask you, it’s much more credible that way, particularly if you can really play one.
I think we’ll put those last few sentences in capitals when we do the transcript here. That’s really good advice.
